newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday mainly due to a rising domestic A share market and more new A share listings, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rocketed to 19.00 percent from 8.21 percent last Friday.
Turnover rose sharply to 9.11 million lots from 7.06 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Many institutions borrowed money on the repo market today to speculate in A shares, pushing up the rates," said a trader. "The listing of two new A share firms also helped."

Shanghai's A share index ended up 5.94 percent to 893.55 points on Monday and the Shenzhen A index rose 0.17 percent. Shangdong Taishan Tourist Ropeway Co and Jiangxi Dongfeng Pharmaceutical Co listed A shares today.

"Rates for early-maturing contracts are likely to continue to rise in the next few days due to more A shares being listed," said a second trader. Shanghai Pudong Stainless Sheet and Haci Co, a magnetic product maker, will list A shares on Wednesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday with institutions selling T-bills to speculate in shares, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, closed down at 119.79 yuan from 120.00 yuan due to heavy institutional selling, traders said.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.51 million lots from 2.46 million.
"The market has become very dull after weeks of falls," one trader said. "Few new investors are entering the market with no recovery likely in the short term."
Traders said even some long-term investors offset their positions today, indicating market sentiment was very weak.
